chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinuri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Baghandi informed me. He said: Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Amr narrated to us from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa from Abu Ishaq from al-Ala' from Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Close the doors to the Mosque except for the door of Ali.

key_terms.الأبواب: The doors - the private doors of houses opening directly into the Prophet's Mosque in Medina
key_terms.المسجد: The mosque - specifically the Prophet's Mosque (al-Masjid al-Nabawi) in Medina
key_terms.باب علي: The door of Ali - Ali ibn Abi Talib's private entrance from his house into the mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the Sadd al-Abwab (closing the doors) hadith narrated by Ibn Umar?
ai.summary: This narration records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) command to close all doors leading into his mosque except that of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Notably, this version is transmitted through an entirely Sunni chain of narration that culminates with the companion Ibn Umar (the son of the second caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab), giving it special significance as it demonstrates that even narrators from outside the Shia tradition transmitted this virtue of Ali. Al-Saduq deliberately included this chain alongside the Shia chains in the same assembly to show the universally acknowledged nature of this prophetic tradition.
